text: reparametrize(x, n_points = NULL) resamples coordinates (numeric @point_data entries) onto uniform arc-length grid linear interpolation. streamline, n_points defaults x@n_points. bundle, defaults rounded mean number points across streamlines, every streamline resampled grid size. bundle_set, bundle reparametrized independently (defaulting, per bundle, rounded mean across bundle’s streamlines). title: The fiber API
text: get_curvature() get_torsion() per-point profile descriptors: fit smoothing splines coordinate along arc-length abscissa, need least four distinct points well defined tract actually curved. perfectly straight segment, curvature identically zero torsion (measures --plane twisting) undefined (NaN). helix good curve illustrate , genuinely curved every direction: add_shape_descriptors(x, descriptors = ...) S7 generic methods streamline, bundle, bundle_set. default descriptors c("euclidean_length", "curvilinear_length", "sinuosity", "curvature", "torsion"). streamline, scalar descriptors land @streamline_data per-point ones @point_data. bundle, scalar descriptors stored length-S vectors bundle@streamline_data; per-point ones (curvature, torsion) stored individual streamline’s @point_data. accessible via subsetting push-. bundle_set, operation applied per bundle, preserving @bundle_data @bundle_set_data. Unknown descriptor names trigger structured cli::cli_warn() message. Note get_curvature() get_torsion() fit cubic smoothing splines therefore need streamline least four distinct points (examples use 10-point streamlines).
code: sl_curve <- streamline(   points = cbind(     X = cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 21)),     Y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 21)),     Z = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 21)   ) ) # Scalar descriptors are fine on any streamline get_euclidean_length(sl1) #> [1] 6.928203 get_curvilinear_length(sl1) #> [1] 6.928203 get_sinuosity(sl1) #> [1] 1  # Per-point profiles are meaningful on a truly curved tract head(get_curvature(sl_curve)) #> [1] 2.547019e-05 2.553796e-02 6.620551e-02 1.142371e-01 1.646170e-01 #> [6] 2.142204e-01 head(get_torsion(sl_curve)) #> [1] -115.1033091    0.5632915    0.4238968    0.4045585    0.4208142 #> [6]    0.4554351 b_long <- bundle(   streamlines = list(     streamline(points = cbind(X = 0:9, Y = 0:9, Z = 0:9)),     streamline(points = cbind(X = 1:10, Y = 1:10, Z = 1:10))   ) ) b_desc <- add_shape_descriptors(b_long) names(b_desc@streamline_data) #> [1] "euclidean_length"   "curvilinear_length" "sinuosity" names(b_desc[[1]]@point_data) #> [1] "curvature" "torsion"

title: The fiber API
text: compute_hausdorff_distance(x, y = NULL) computes symmetric Hausdorff distance. dispatches four cases: core pairwise computation implemented C++ (via cpp11). Coordinates coerced double precision passed compiled code, integer-stored @points matrices (e.g. built X = 1:5) handled correctly. Unsupported x types (invalid y) produce clear error via catch-method.
code: sb <- streamline(points = cbind(X = 0:4, Y = 0:4, Z = 0:4)) sc <- streamline(points = cbind(X = 1:5, Y = 1:5, Z = 1:5))  # streamline x streamline -> scalar compute_hausdorff_distance(sb, sc) #> [1] 1.732051  # bundle x missing -> dist object bd <- bundle(streamlines = list(sb, sc)) as.matrix(compute_hausdorff_distance(bd)) #>          1        2 #> 1 0.000000 1.732051 #> 2 1.732051 0.000000  # bundle x streamline -> vector compute_hausdorff_distance(bd, sb) #> [1] 0.000000 1.732051  # bundle x bundle -> combined dist object bd2 <- bundle(streamlines = list(sc)) as.matrix(compute_hausdorff_distance(bd, bd2)) #>          1        2        3 #> 1 0.000000 1.732051 1.732051 #> 2 1.732051 0.000000 0.000000 #> 3 1.732051 0.000000 0.000000

title: The fiber API
text: as_streamline(x) returns streamline: streamline → returned unchanged (identity). bundle → sole streamline (errors bundle ≠ 1 streamlines). dwiFiber (dti) → single fiber streamline (errors multi-fiber; use as_bundle() instead). as_bundle(x) returns bundle: streamline → single-element bundle (lossless). bundle → returned unchanged (identity). dwiFiber → fiber becomes streamline. Per-point direction vectors (columns 4–6 @fibers) stored @point_data$direction_x/y/z. Tracking metadata (method, minfa, maxangle) become scalars @bundle_data; vector metadata (ddim, ddim0, voxelext, orientation) expanded individual scalar entries (e.g. voxelext_1, voxelext_2, voxelext_3). as_bundle_set(x) returns bundle_set: bundle_set → returned unchanged (identity). bundle → single-element bundle_set; optional name argument sets element name. as_dwifiber(x) converts streamline bundle dwiFiber S4 class dti. requires dti package installed. Per-point directions taken @point_data$direction_x/y/z present, otherwise estimated coordinates via finite differences (forward / backward ends, central elsewhere), unit-normalised. Bundled metadata method, minfa, maxangle, level, source transferred corresponding dwiFiber slots present. Note dti loads rgl package startup, calling coercion functions environment without graphics display can print rgl warning (e.g. 'rgl.init' failed X11 error). warning comes rgl, fiber, affect conversion.
code: if (requireNamespace("dti", quietly = TRUE)) {   dfi <- as_dwifiber(bd)   class(dfi)   # round-trip   as_bundle(dfi)@n_streamlines } #> [1] 2

title: Getting started with fiber
text: streamline stores $P \times 3$ matrix coordinates. columns must named "X", "Y", "Z". can attach per-point attributes (e.g. fractional anisotropy) via point_data per-streamline scalars (e.g. mean FA label) via streamline_data:
code: # A helix in 3-D, sampled at 50 points t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 50) sl <- streamline(   points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)) ) sl #>  #> ── Object of class `fiber::streamline()` with 50 points. ── #>  #> • Point attributes: none #> • Streamline attributes: none #> sl <- streamline(   points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)),   point_data = list(FA = runif(50)),   streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(runif(50)), label = "helix") ) sl@n_points # 50 #> [1] 50 sl@point_attributes # "FA" #> [1] "FA" sl@streamline_attributes # c("mean_FA", "label") #> [1] "mean_FA" "label"

title: S7 Data Structures for Diffusion MRI Tractography
text: streamline stores: @points — numeric matrix size P×3P \times 3 (number points three spatial dimensions). columns must named "X", "Y", "Z". @point_data — named list numeric-vectors length PP (number points). Stores additional per-point attributes (e.g. fractional anisotropy). @streamline_data — named list per-streamline scalars (length-1 values, type, e.g. mean FA character label). bundle stores: @streamlines — list streamline objects. @streamline_data — named list per-streamline vectors length SS (number streamlines). Attributes common streamlines lifted automatically construction time pushed back individual streamlines subsetting. @bundle_data — named list bundle-level scalars (length-1 values, type). bundle_set stores: @bundles — list bundle objects (optionally named, e.g. white-matter bundle labels "callosum" subject session IDs "sub-01", case names transferred per-bundle attribute @bundle_data called id_from_input_names). @bundle_data — named list per-bundle vectors length BB (number bundles). Attributes common bundles lifted automatically construction time pushed back individual bundles subsetting. @bundle_set_data — named list set-level scalars (length-1 values, type).

title: fiber: 'S7' Data Structures for Diffusion MRI Tractography — fiber-package
text: Provides three S7 classes — streamline, bundle, bundle_set — representing diffusion MRI tractography data R, together concise set methods computing shape descriptors (arc-length, curvature, torsion, sinuosity), Hausdorff distance streamlines, arc-length reparametrization streamlines bundles onto uniform grids, combination streamlines bundles single bundle, combination bundles multiple subjects sessions bundle_set, coercion dwiFiber S4 class 'dti' package.
